newsitem.title: UK: UK's Rifkind says Horam in line with policy.
newsitem.headline: UK's Rifkind says Horam in line with policy.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind denied on Tuesday that a junior health minister's comments on the single European currency were out of line with government policy.
Junior health minister John Horam said in his election manifesto that he personally opposed a single currency but he thought the right line was to stay at the negotiating table.
The remark was immediately seized on by government critics as evidence that the ruling Conseravtives were hopelessly split over the single currency.
Rifkind, however, told BBC radio that Horam had made "a perfectly reasonable statement fully in line with government policy".
Rifkind added: "The government policy, supported by 72 percent of the electorate, is that we must negotiate and decide.

"Mr Horam has said explicitly that he believes the time to reach a decision on the single currency will be at the end of the negotiations and when the government will decide." -- Lonondon Newsroom +44-171-542-7947
